summary: Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, Lobsang Gyatso studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso. He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1973, serving as its head from ~1973 to 1997.

A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, Lobsang Jamspal earned degrees at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and a Ph.D. at Columbia under Alex Wayman. His appointments include posts at Delhi, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia (attested 1985–1990).

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Drubwang Shakya Shri, Shukseb Jetsun Choying Zangmo, Pema Chok Palzangpo, Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Lhundrub Tsondru.

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Lobsang Shastri served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Working in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Lobsang Tendzin studied at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries under Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa and the 14th Dalai Lama. He directed the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1988–2000).

Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy degree at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Lobsang Tenzin studied at Drepung Monastery. He served as Principal (1971) and Director (1988–2001) of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and later became Chancellor of Sanchi University of Buddhist-Indic Studies.

A Tibetology and history scholar, Lobsang Yongdan studied at Kumbum Monastery and Cambridge (PhD 2014) under Hildegard Diemberger. He held fellowships at the Max Planck Institute (2016), University of Bonn (2016–2020), and Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2026).

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Loden Sherab Dagyab studied at Drepung Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as Director of Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966) and Tibetologist at the University of Bonn (1966).
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Lodrö Sangpo studied under supervisor Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, Lokesh Chandra studied at Punjab University and Utrecht (Ph.D. under Jan Gonda). He served as Director of the International Academy of Indian Culture (~1963–2022) and President of the ICCR (2014–2017).
Active in Buddhist studies, Longlian studied under Fazun beginning in 1939 and under the traditional teacher Nenghai Shi from approximately 1941 to 1967.

A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Lore Sander studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1960–1967). She was a Curator at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and taught at the Free University of Berlin (1994).

A Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar, Lori Meeks studied at Columbia (BA) and Princeton (PhD under Jacqueline I. Stone). After a fellowship at Stanford (~2003–2004), she became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at USC in 2004.

A scholar in religious studies and Indology, Loriliai Biernacki studied under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (~1994–1999). She later held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder, becoming Associate Professor around 2007.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Lorna Dewaraja studied at the University of Ceylon (~1948–1952) and University of London (~1966–1969). She served as Associate Professor of History at the University of Peradeniya and taught at Colombo.

A Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar, Ledderose studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne. He served as Professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010) and President of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

A Sinologist and archaeologist, Lothar von Falkenhausen studied at Bonn, Peking University, Kyoto, and Harvard (PhD ~1982–1988). He taught at UC Riverside (~1990–1993) and became a Full Professor at UCLA in 1993.

A scholar of Iranian-Central Asian studies and linguistics, Casartelli studied at Ushaw, London, and KU Leuven under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin. He was Professor at KU Leuven (1900–1903) and Lecturer in Iranian languages at Manchester (1903–1920).
